subject: maths
source_note: Topic structure follows the National Curriculum KS3 programme of study for Mathematics. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships.

units.name: Number
units.blurb: Place value, the four operations, powers, roots and percentages

units.name: Algebra
units.blurb: Notation, expressions, equations, graphs and sequences

units.name: Ratio, Proportion & Rates of Change
units.blurb: Ratio, proportion, percentage change and compound units

units.name: Geometry & Measures
units.blurb: Area, volume, angles, transformations and Pythagoras

units.name: Probability
units.blurb: Outcomes, sample spaces and the probability scale

topics.name: Place Value

topics.name: Ordering Numbers
topics.blurb: Ordering integers, decimals and fractions; inequality symbols

topics.name: Factors & Multiples

topics.name: The Four Operations
topics.blurb: Operations with positive and negative integers, decimals and fractions

topics.name: Order of Operations
topics.blurb: Brackets, powers, roots, reciprocals and inverse operations

topics.name: Powers, Roots & Standard Form
topics.blurb: Integer powers, real roots and numbers in standard form

topics.name: Fractions & Decimals
topics.blurb: Working between terminating decimals and their fractions

topics.name: Percentages
topics.blurb: Percentages, percentage change and fractions as operators

topics.name: Rounding & Estimation
topics.blurb: Standard units, rounding, estimation and error bounds

topics.name: Algebraic Notation
topics.blurb: Conventions of algebraic notation and substitution into formulae

topics.name: Manipulating Expressions
topics.blurb: Collecting like terms, expanding brackets and factorising

topics.name: Formulae
topics.blurb: Standard formulae and changing the subject

topics.name: Linear Equations
topics.blurb: Solving linear equations in one variable

topics.name: Coordinates & Graphs
topics.blurb: Coordinates in four quadrants and graphs of linear and quadratic functions

topics.name: Straight-Line Graphs
topics.blurb: Gradients, intercepts, y = mx + c and simultaneous equations

topics.name: Sequences
topics.blurb: Generating sequences, arithmetic nth terms and geometric sequences

topics.name: Units & Scale
topics.blurb: Converting standard units and using scale factors, diagrams and maps

topics.name: Ratio
topics.blurb: Ratio notation, simplest form and dividing in a given ratio

topics.name: Proportion
topics.blurb: Direct and inverse proportion, graphically and algebraically

topics.name: Percentage Change & Interest
topics.blurb: Percentage increase, decrease, original value and simple interest

topics.name: Compound Units
topics.blurb: Speed, density and unit pricing

topics.name: Area & Volume
topics.blurb: Perimeter, area and volume formulae including circles and prisms

topics.name: Constructions & Drawing
topics.blurb: Measuring and drawing figures and ruler-and-compass constructions

topics.name: Properties of Shapes
topics.blurb: Properties of triangles, quadrilaterals, circles and 3-D solids

topics.name: Transformations
topics.blurb: Translations, rotations, reflections and enlargement

topics.name: Angles
topics.blurb: Angle facts, parallel lines and angle sums of polygons

topics.name: Pythagoras & Trigonometry
topics.blurb: Congruence, similarity, Pythagoras' Theorem and trigonometric ratios

topics.name: Probability Basics
topics.blurb: Frequency of outcomes and the 0–1 probability scale summing to 1

topics.name: Sets & Sample Spaces
topics.blurb: Venn diagrams and theoretical sample spaces for combined events

topics.name: Averages & Spread
topics.blurb: Mean, median, mode, range and outliers

topics.name: Charts & Diagrams
topics.blurb: Tables, bar charts, pie charts and pictograms

topics.name: Bivariate Data
topics.blurb: Relationships between two variables and scatter graphs

connections.why: Place value underpins formal written methods for the four operations
Ordering numbers relies on understanding their place value
HCF and LCM are used to simplify and add fractions
Combining operations requires the priority of operations
Powers and roots sit within the order-of-operations hierarchy
Percentages are interpreted as equivalent fractions and decimals
Algebra generalises the structure of arithmetic operations
Notation conventions are needed to collect terms and expand brackets
Rearranging formulae uses the same manipulation skills
Solving equations rearranges and simplifies expressions
Linear equations in two variables become straight-line graphs
Plotting in the Cartesian plane lets us read gradients and intercepts
Percentage change problems apply percentages multiplicatively
Ratios and fractions both express multiplicative relationships
Proportional reasoning extends the language of ratio
Speed and density are rates built from proportional relationships
Direct proportion is a straight line through the origin
Angle facts derive the properties of polygons and shapes
Congruence and similarity lead to Pythagoras and trigonometry
Pythagoras' Theorem uses squares and square roots
Area and volume require fluent conversion between units
Sample spaces give the theoretical probabilities of outcomes
Charts display the distributions that averages summarise
Scatter graphs extend data display to two variables
